steps.description: The hypothesis distinguishes between rigid and fat function families based on whether a small neural network can achieve zero violation (≤1e-3) on held-out constraints. The previous iteration (iter 20) used an exponential function for the rigid family which failed to converge, likely due to the scale mismatch (the exponential grows rapidly, making the 1e-3 tolerance impossible to meet without normalization). The world model also flagged the exponential as a potential fat family (infinite-dimensional representation). We need to re-examine the families: the rigid family should be a low-dimensional polynomial space (e.g., first-order PDE solution with finite basis), and the fat family should be an analytic class requiring high capacity. We'll explore using symbolic methods to define proper families and run capacity scans with appropriate normalization.
